translation.title: Povidone-Iodine Ointment
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for the germicidal disinfection of torn wounds, burns, wounds, pressure sores, ulcers, abscesses, infected skin surfaces, and injection and catheter sites.
translation.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day. Cover it with a dressing or bandage if needed.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, in newborns and infants under 6 months, before or after radioactive iodine treatment, if you have thyroid dysfunction such as nodular goiter, endemic goiter or Hashimoto's thyroiditis, if you have kidney failure, or if you have dermatitis herpetiformis. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, if you are severely ill (such as burn patients), or if you have experienced thyroid disease or kidney failure. Do not use it in the eyes or take it by mouth. Be careful not to let the undiluted solution get into the eyes; if it does, rinse them immediately with clean water. Wash the affected area clean and disinfect it. When using it on severe wounds, use distilled water for injection or sterile purified water as the diluent; do not use tap water or ordinary purified water. If it gets on clothing, it can be washed off easily with water if washed immediately; on synthetic fibers, it can be removed with ammonia water or sodium thiosulfate solution. Soaps weaken the germicidal action, so wash them off thoroughly before using this medicine. If it was used just before childbirth, wash the newborn's eyes and bathe the baby as soon as possible after delivery so that the medicine does not remain on the skin. Patients with extensive burns should receive sufficient fluids when using it. When using it on ulcers caused by burns, use it only on ulcers from secondary damage after the burn — do not use it on fresh burns. Leave an interval of 1 to 2 weeks between using this medicine and scintigraphy. If an infection such as peritonitis or osteomyelitis occurs, wash the area with physiological saline before using this medicine. If the iodine in this medicine is absorbed through healthy or damaged skin, it can interfere with thyroid function tests. Do not use it together with lithium treatment or hydrogen peroxide; consult a doctor or pharmacist when using it with chlorhexidine, silver sulfadiazine compounds, alkali- or mercury-containing preparations, or enzyme-based wound treatments. Occasionally pain, itching, irritation, a rash, redness or dermatitis may occur; if these symptoms are severe, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if rare reactions occur, such as hypersensitivity (difficulty breathing, flushing, hives), a burning feeling, skin ulcers, contact dermatitis, skin discoloration, metabolic acidosis or abnormal kidney function. Rarely, anaphylactic symptoms or shock may occur: if severe symptoms such as sudden itching, swelling and heartburn appear together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat or shortness of breath, stop use immediately and see a doctor. If used inside the vagina, blood levels of inorganic iodine and total iodine may rise.
